page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 64-bit ARM-based instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 64 dedicated physical cores running AWS Neoverse-N1 (ARMv8) processors clocked at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. For high-speed temporary storage, it features 3,800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in multi-threaded and I/O-intensive workloads. Multi-core performance is robust, demonstrated by top-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng tests, Clang software compilation, and cached small-block memory bandwidth reaching 3,782.85 GB/sec. Data-layer performance is equally pronounced, yielding 72.77 million Redis SET operations per second and 45.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded throughput shows lower relative potency, with Geekbench single-core, gzip compression, and single-threaded decompression scoring in the lower quartile.

With its combination of dense multi-core processing, substantial memory, and high-capacity NVMe storage, the m6gd.16xlarge offers high resource density without the licensing premiums typical of legacy instruction sets. The architecture is best aligned with concurrent web services, distributed caching systems like Redis, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional database environments that capitalize on local fast storage rather than heavy single-threaded compute.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud server powered by 64 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 256 GB of RAM, 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 25 Gbps baseline networking, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory profile without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded scaling, excelling in Clang software compilation, multi-core stress testing, static web serving throughput, and key-value datastores with over 72 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution speed and large-model inference remain modest. With its integrated high-speed ephemeral NVMe array and high core count, the m6gd.16xlarge offers cost-efficient multi-tenant density well suited for distributed microservices, CI/CD build farms, caching layers, and high-throughput data processing workloads.
